_policy.rule: Every localized tool, legal page, metadata string, and runtime message must use these exact terms for these concepts. Numbers keep the English source format: period decimal separators and the existing unit spacing.

voltage drop.gloss: Voltage lost along a conductor because it has resistance.

one-way distance.gloss: Distance from the source to the load only; never the return path.

round trip.gloss: The complete outgoing and return current path.

ampacity.gloss: Maximum current a conductor can carry under stated conditions.

conductor.gloss: A wire or other material that carries electric current.

largest conductor.gloss: The physically largest conductor size present; in AWG, a smaller gauge number means a larger conductor.

wire size / gauge.gloss: The standardized cross-sectional size designation of a wire.

branch circuit.gloss: Circuit from the final overcurrent device to its outlets or loads.

feeder.gloss: Conductors carrying power from service equipment to downstream distribution.

panel.gloss: Distribution panel containing breakers or other protective devices.

sub-panel.gloss: A downstream distribution panel supplied by a feeder.

breaker / overcurrent device.gloss: A device that opens a circuit when current exceeds its permitted value.
breaker / overcurrent device.fr-CA: disjoncteur / dispositif de protection contre les surintensités
breaker / overcurrent device.zh-Hans: 断路器 / 过电流保护装置

grounding conductor.gloss: Conductor used to provide the grounding or bonding fault-current path.
grounding conductor.fr-CA: conducteur de mise à la terre

neutral.gloss: Grounded circuit conductor connected to the system neutral point.

phase.gloss: One alternating-current waveform or energized system leg.

load.gloss: Equipment or demand that consumes electrical power.

continuous load.gloss: A load expected to operate continuously for the code-defined duration.

derating.gloss: Reducing usable ampacity because of heat, bundling, or other conditions.

ambient temperature.gloss: Temperature of the surrounding air or environment.

terminal temperature rating.gloss: Maximum temperature rating permitted by the connected terminal.

box fill.gloss: Code calculation limiting conductors and devices inside an electrical box.

conduit fill.gloss: Code calculation limiting conductor area inside a raceway.

service.gloss: The electrical supply connection and equipment at the building entrance.

mandatory.gloss: Required by the governing rule, not optional.

recommendation.gloss: Advised for good practice but not generally enforceable.

within the limit.gloss: At or below a stated maximum.

should.gloss: Expresses advice rather than a requirement.

equipment grounding conductor.gloss: The conductor that carries equipment fault current back toward the source.
equipment grounding conductor.es: conductor de puesta a tierra de equipos
equipment grounding conductor.fr-CA: conducteur de mise à la terre de l’équipement

current-carrying conductor.gloss: An insulated conductor that normally carries load current.

termination.gloss: A conductor connection point whose temperature rating can limit usable ampacity.

rated for.gloss: Having an approved nominal capacity for the stated duty.

explain themselves.gloss: Brand promise that each calculator shows how its own result was obtained; it does not mean merely that the interface is self-explanatory.
explain themselves.es: muestran cómo se obtiene cada resultado
explain themselves.fr-CA: montrent comment chaque résultat est obtenu
explain themselves.zh-Hans: 展示每项结果的计算过程

correction factor.gloss: Multiplier used to change ampacity for ambient temperature.

adjustment factor.gloss: Multiplier used to change ampacity for the number of conductors.

termination temperature rating.gloss: Temperature rating of a conductor connection that limits final usable ampacity.

bonding conductor.gloss: A conductor that provides the low-impedance fault-current bond between metal parts; CEC Rule 4-004 excludes it from the derating count.

power and lighting conductors.gloss: The CEC category of installed insulated conductors considered for the Rule 4-004 derating count, subject to the rule's neutral and bonding exclusions.

spare conductor.gloss: An installed conductor reserved for possible future use and not presently connected to a load.
